page: UpCloud GPU-48xCPU-960GB-4xH100 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by 48 shared Intel Xeon 8462Y+ physical cores running at 2.0 GHz on a KVM hypervisor. The system features 960.0 GB of system memory, providing 20.0 GB per core. Acceleration is driven by four NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs, delivering a total of 320 GB of VRAM. Local storage is not bundled with this instance type, meaning external storage solutions must be attached.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core and memory performance. The server achieved a passmark CPU score of 85426.66, placing it in the top tier, and a multi-core stress-ng score of 96293.69. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with small-block cached reads reaching 7649.82 GB/sec and large-block uncached reads at 316.04 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, the system processed 10308.98 tokens per second for prompt processing and 377.14 tokens per second for text generation using a small 135M LLM model.

The qualitative cost profile of this server reflects a high-density hardware configuration, trading off dedicated CPU allocation for shared vCPUs. This shared CPU model may introduce performance variability under sustained non-GPU compute loads, though the massive GPU and memory resources offset this for accelerator-dependent tasks. Given the 320 GB of VRAM and 960 GB of system memory, this instance is configured for large-scale machine learning, LLM inference, data science pipelines, and parallelized scientific computing.

Operating on a KVM hypervisor, this instance does not include local storage. In benchmark testing, the server demonstrated top-tier capabilities, scoring 85426.66 on PassMark CPU and achieving a multi-core stress-ng score of 96293.69. While the shared CPU allocation presents a potential tradeoff for sustained host-CPU workloads, the massive GPU memory and system RAM density make this configuration highly efficient for large-scale machine learning inference, deep learning training, and complex data science workloads.
